confidence_notes: Beer, coffee and meal anchors come from aggregated crowd-sourced indexes found in web searches (Numbeo's Pai page, Expat Exchange, CityCost and similar). Those indexes put an inexpensive meal at about 40-100 THB, a domestic draft pint at about 72 THB, a cappuccino at about 60-70 THB and a mid-range dinner for two at about 650-810 THB. The Numbeo Pai data looks dated and is crowd-sourced. I rounded up slightly for tourist-oriented Pai venues and used about 32-33 THB per USD. My searches found no reliable Pai-specific prices for cocktails or wine by the glass. Cocktail and wine are therefore estimated from the local beer price, assuming a cocktail costs about 1.7 times a beer and a glass of wine about 1.8 times, because imported wine is costly in Thailand. The four accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Pai's backpacker and bungalow market. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any listings. Seasonal swings are large, and peak season (roughly Nov-Feb) can push accommodation and drink prices noticeably higher.
comparable_city_reasoning: Pai is a small northern Thai backpacker and tourism town, so I used Pai-specific index data where it existed. Where it didn't (cocktails, wine, accommodation), I based estimates on typical Chiang Mai-area and northern Thailand budget-tourism pricing, discounted slightly for Pai's lower-cost, bungalow-dominated lodging.
